prov.text: Provision for Credit Losses. The Company recorded no provision for credit losses for the three and six months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025. The absence of a provision in the current periods reflected the continued adequacy of the allowance for credit losses, as determined through management’s evaluation of economic forecast assumptions and other qualitative and quantitative factors. Expected loss estimates incorporated borrower and portfolio-level factors, including client-specific information, changes in risk ratings, projected delinquencies, and the potential impact of economic conditions on borrowers' ability to repay. While the provision for credit losses remained unchanged, the Company did see an increase in nonperforming assets which was primarily due to an increase in nonaccrual commercial real estate loans during the six months ended, September 30, 2026. Net recoveries totaled $374,000 and $462,000 for the three and six months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to net recoveries of $1,000 and $53,000 for the same periods in 2025.

nonint.text: Non-Interest Expense. Non-interest expense increased $713,000 and $1.9 million to $12.9 million and $25.8 million for the three and six months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to the same periods in the prior year. The increase was primarily attributable to higher salaries and employee benefits expense, which increased $845,000 and $1.6 million for the three and six months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, primarily due to increased compensation and employee benefit costs associated with strategic investments in the Company's leadership structure and growth initiatives, as well as higher insurance premiums. Data processing expense increased $119,000 and $289,000 for the three and six months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to the same periods in the prior year, reflecting continued investment in technology to support the Company's growth initiatives. State and local taxes increased by $113,000 and $231,000 for the three and six months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, primarily due to higher business and occupation taxes resulting from changes in state tax requirements and increased sales tax activity related to projects supporting the Company's strategic initiatives.

nonop.text: Interest Expense. Interest expense totaled $5.0 million and $10.0 million for the three and six months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $5.6 million and $11.1 million for the three and six months ended September 30, 2025, respectively. The decreases were primarily attributable to lower interest expense on FHLB advances, driven by both lower average balances and lower rates, partially offset by higher interest expense on deposits.

tax.text: Income Taxes. The provision for income taxes was $539,000 and $974,000 for the three and six months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to $296,000 and $618,000 for the corresponding periods in the prior year. The increase in income tax expense was primarily attributable to higher pre-tax income. The Company's effective tax rate was 21.5% and 21.0% for the three and six months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to 21.2% and 21.0% for the corresponding periods ended September 30, 2025. Management continues to believe that the Company's deferred tax assets are fully realizable; therefore, no valuation allowance was required as of September 30, 2026. Net deferred tax assets totaled $14.2 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $12.1 million at March 31, 2026.

net.text: Net Income. Net income was $2.0 million, or $0.10 per diluted share, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $1.1 million, or $0.05 per diluted share, for the same period in the prior year. Net income for the six months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 was $3.7 million or $0.18 per diluted share and $2.3 million or $0.11 per diluted share, respectively. The increases in net income for three and six months ended September 30, 2026 were primarily due to increases in net interest income of $2.0 million and $3.6 million, respectively, partially offset by increases in non-interest expense of $713,000 and $1.9 million, respectively. The increases in net interest income reflected higher interest and dividend income of $1.5 million and $2.5 million, and decreases in interest expense on borrowings of $609,000 and $1.8 million, partially offset by increases in interest expense on deposits of $45,000 and $632,000, respectively.

capex.text: The Company incurs capital expenditures on an ongoing basis to expand and improve its product offerings, enhance and modernize its technology infrastructure, and to introduce new technology-based products to compete effectively in its markets. The Company evaluates capital expenditure projects based on a variety of factors, including expected strategic impacts (such as forecasted impact on revenue growth, productivity, expenses, service levels and client retention) and its expected return on investment. The amount of capital investment is influenced by, among other things, current and projected demand for its services and products, cash flow generated by operating activities, cash required for other purposes and regulatory considerations. Based on its current capital allocation objectives, during the remainder of fiscal 2027 the Company expects cash expenditures of approximately $1.7 million for capital investment in premises and equipment.

Net interest income.text: Net Interest Income. The Company’s profitability depends primarily on its net interest income, which is the difference between the income it receives on interest-earning assets and the interest paid on deposits and borrowings. When the rate earned on interest-earning assets equals or exceeds the rate paid on interest-bearing liabilities, a positive interest rate spread will generate net interest income. The Company’s results of operations are also significantly affected by general economic and competitive conditions, particularly changes in market interest rates, government legislation and regulation, and monetary and fiscal policies.

intro.text: Riverview Bancorp, Inc., a Washington corporation, is the bank holding company of Riverview Bank. At March 31, 2026, the Company had total assets of $1.46 billion, total deposits of $1.25 billion and total shareholders’ equity of $145.6 million. The Company’s executive offices are located in Vancouver, Washington. The Bank has two subsidiaries, Riverview Trust Company (the “Trust Company”) and Riverview Services, Inc. (“Riverview Services”). The Trust Company is a trust and financial services company located in downtown Vancouver, Washington, and provides full-service brokerage activities, trust and asset management services. Riverview Services acts as a trustee for deeds of trust on mortgage loans granted by the Bank and receives a reconveyance fee for each deed of trust.
